rv.q: Now, I honestly can't find fault with it.
This is one of those shows where the funny bits are so funny, so merrily rude or un-PC, it can make the less gag-stuffed moments seem wan by comparison.
A carnival of wisecracks and witty tunes, the show is all about a Broadway producer's outrageous bid to engineer a dead-cert flop
Fortunately, original helmer-choreographer Susan Stroman was on hand to restore some kick and bite to the all-time biggest Tony winner, and a fine time was to be had.
If you want non-stop giggles, gloriously provocative jokes and an easy escape from everyday misery, there's no better place to be right now than the Garrick.
Trevor Ashley is perfectly cast as the scene-stealing director Roger De Bris…Harry Morrison also gives a stand-out performance.
I'm not sure anything new is achieved with this production, but then, that's always been the case with The Producers onstage.
All in all, this is a musical that still guarantees laugh after laugh after laugh, with a genuinely brilliant score from Brooks.
Whatever it is that was missing has certainly been found this time around, as the West End transfer is an obvious five-star show.
Outrageous, audacious and utterly unmissable, this West End revival is a triumph of impeccable casting, razor-sharp direction and a laugh-a-minute script.
Everyone has enormous fun and so, in consequence, we do too
The Producers really is an outstanding collective production where every performer shows up and delivers.
